job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

passage: In our science club today, we analyzed the history of India's lunar exploration. We learned that Chandrayaan-1 was a major milestone, but it did not carry a rover; instead, it used the M3 instrument, provided by NASA, to detect water molecules trapped in lunar soil. This is very different from liquid water; it exists only as trace amounts of ice or hydrated minerals in shadowed regions. Moving to Chandrayaan-2, we discussed the landing sequence. Unlike on Earth, where thick atmospheres allow the use of parachutes to create drag, the Moon has no atmosphere. Therefore, the Vikram lander had to use retro-rockets to reduce its speed for a soft landing. We also clarified that while the Vikram lander faced challenges, the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter remained operational in its orbit, continuing to send valuable data back to Earth. Finally, we looked at Chandrayaan-3, which successfully touched down near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023. This mission proved that India could achieve a controlled landing, with the Pragyan rover performing experiments for one lunar day before its mission concluded. These missions show that lunar exploration requires precise engineering to overcome the lack of atmosphere and the harsh conditions of the lunar surface.

items.evidence: We learned that Chandrayaan-1 was a major milestone, but it did not carry a rover; instead, it used the M3 instrument, provided by NASA, to detect water molecules trapped in lunar soil.
items.q: How did Chandrayaan-1 find signs of water on the Moon?
options: Using the M3 instrument supplied by NASA
Using a rover that drove over the soil
Using the M3 instrument built by ISRO
Using a probe that landed softly on the soil
items.explain: Chandrayaan-1 carried no rover; it used the M3 instrument, provided by NASA, to detect water molecules in lunar soil.

wrong.why: thinks ISRO built the M3 instrument
thinks a probe landed softly and tested the soil

items.evidence: This is very different from liquid water; it exists only as trace amounts of ice or hydrated minerals in shadowed regions.
items.q: Ananya says Chandrayaan-1 found water, so astronauts could drink from Moon lakes. What does the lesson say about this water?
options: The water is only tiny traces of ice in soil
The water is in lakes but too cold to drink
The water is liquid and safe to drink directly
The water flows freely in the sunlit regions
items.explain: The Moon's water is not liquid; it exists only as trace amounts of ice or hydrated minerals in shadowed regions.

wrong.why: thinks the Moon has lakes of water
thinks Moon water is ready drinking water
thinks liquid water can stay on the surface

items.evidence: Unlike on Earth, where thick atmospheres allow the use of parachutes to create drag, the Moon has no atmosphere.
items.q: A team plans to slow its Moon lander with a huge parachute. What will happen?
options: It will not slow it, since there is no air
It will slow the lander gently, like on Earth
It will work, but only near the south pole
It will slow it only if it is big enough
items.explain: Parachutes need air to create drag. The Moon has no atmosphere, so a parachute cannot slow the lander.

wrong.why: thinks parachutes work on the Moon as on Earth
grabs the south pole detail from the passage
thinks a bigger parachute can fix the problem

items.evidence: We also clarified that while the Vikram lander faced challenges, the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter remained operational in its orbit, continuing to send valuable data back to Earth.
items.q: Vikram ran into trouble while landing. What happened to the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter after that?
options: It kept circling the Moon and sending data
It crashed onto the Moon along with Vikram
It landed in Vikram's place to finish the job
It stopped working and fell back to Earth
items.explain: Even though Vikram faced challenges, the orbiter stayed working in orbit and kept sending valuable data to Earth.

wrong.why: thinks the orbiter crashed with Vikram
mixes up the roles of orbiter and lander
thinks one failure ended the whole mission

items.evidence: This mission proved that India could achieve a controlled landing, with the Pragyan rover performing experiments for one lunar day before its mission concluded.
items.q: Kabir says Pragyan is still exploring the Moon today. What does the lesson show about Pragyan's work?
options: It ran tests for one lunar day, then ended
It has kept running tests for many years
It never ran tests, as there was no rover
It ran tests for months after a hard landing
items.explain: Pragyan performed experiments for only one lunar day before its mission concluded, so it is not still exploring.

wrong.why: thinks Pragyan is a permanent rover
mixes up which mission carried no rover
confuses Pragyan with the impact probe
